chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, all from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The Kalalah is one who has neither a son nor a father.

key_terms.الْكَلَالَةُ: Kalalah: A person who dies leaving neither a direct descendant (son) nor a direct ascendant (father).

ai.seo_question: What is the definition of Kalalah in Shia inheritance jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This concise definition from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes the foundational criterion for 'Kalalah' as the absence of both direct descendants (awlād) and direct ascendants (wālid), a key distinction in Shia jurisprudence for determining inheritance shares among collateral relatives. It directly elucidates the condition mentioned in Surah An-Nisa, clarifying that the specific rules for Kalala apply only when these primary lines of succession are extinct.
